newsitem.title: USA: P&G says Q2 N.America sales up, Asia sales off.
newsitem.headline: P&G says Q2 N.America sales up, Asia sales off.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co said Tuesday its North American sales grew three percent in the second quarter ended December 31 versus the year-ago quarter.
Unit volume in North America, sparked by double digit growth in the laundry business, grew five percent, P&G said, adding it set a North American shipment record.

In Asia, net earnings rose 12 percent but unit volume declined seven percent and sales declined eight percent, P&G said. Exchange rates, competitive pressures and a continuing inventory, retail shelf management and promotions program had negative impact, the company said in its quarterly statement.

The consumer products giant said that in North America, the difference between sales and unit volume growth was largely due to price reductions for lower commodity costs. Capacity constraints, especially in paper tissue and towels, continued, it said.
North American net earnings grew 15 percent, helped by lower commodity prices, primarily pulp, P&G said.
In its Europe/Middle East/Africa region, P&G said unit volume grew four percent but sales were stable, reflecting unfavorable exchange rate movements.
Net earnings in that region grew 24 percent versus the year-ago quarter, reflecting lower costs especially on pulp.

In Latin America, unit volume was off three percent versus the year-ago period due to continued economic difficulties in several markets, but sales grew three percent due to pricing which was designed to address inflation and devaluation, particularly in Mexico, P&G said.
P&G said Latin America net earnings increased 35 percent on improved margins, reflecting pricing and cost reductions.
As reported, P&G posted overall second quarter earnings of $1.35 a primary share versus $1.18 a year ago.
